arguments.reason: The only recorded verification is sha256:9d24463217d47102ba1bc9422eb929d89979b8dd24d2de4695c1480b81cbb178, which is explicitly self-scoped: its own derivation states it is a "Structural marker/spec/token check only" and that the "Standalone AST/API verification and fallible review remain required before conformance." So the three-part acceptance conjunction is not yet discharged: (1) the structural checker agrees, but (2) the supplied standalone AST/API checker has not run against the script, and (3) the scripted fallible review has not run, so no severity has been observed. The produced artifact status is "partial" and it carries an explicit unresolved list noting the AST/API checker and review are unrun and that Blender 5.2 was never executed. Concrete defects are also visible from inspection and warrant a changed pass rather than an identical resubmission: (a) camera targeting is wrong in the script - `look_at(camera, [10.0, -14.0, 8.0])`-style code passes the camera's own intended location as the target for S02 and S03 frames (the script calls look_at with [-4.0,-6.0,2.8] and [7.0,-10.0,2.0], i.e. the camera positions), while the spec requires targets [0,0,1], [1.2,0.5,1.2], and [0,0,1.5]; (b) the courier rotation is hardcoded via math.radians(0.0)/math.radians(45.0) rather than sourced from the embedded SHOT_SPEC value_end, so the literal spec and the constructed values can drift; (c) cube sizing uses the primitive size parameter plus obj.scale, which requires confirmation against the narrow AST grammar since `scale` is only permitted as a receiver attribute, and the declared dimensions must actually be applied; (d) the S01 'drone excluded from visible subjects' constraint is stated but never enforced (no hide/view-layer handling), which is a spec-versus-script behavioral gap.
arguments.stop_rule: Choose substantive STOP only when all three acceptance checks pass: the host structural checker passes, the supplied standalone AST/API checker passes on the script, and the scripted fallible review returns no high-severity issue, with no artifact missing and no unaddressed defect offering a stated prospect of a fix. Continue with another route/spawn/assemble/verify pass whenever a hard check fails, the reviewer leaves a high-severity issue, an artifact is missing, or another pass has a stated prospect of fixing the defect. Resource stops (logical-call ceiling, owner spend ceiling via max_spend_usd, missing priced usage) and concrete instrument failures are distinct from substantive STOP and are never called exhaustion. OR stop early only if a resource guard or instrument failure halts the run, reported as such and not as exhaustion.
arguments.what_changes_next: Rerun a full assemble/verify pass with these changes: (1) fix `look_at` targets so each shot aims at its declared target - S01 [0,0,1] at frame 1, S02 [1.2,0.5,1.2] at frame 97, S03 [0,0,1.5] at frame 169 - keyframing both rotation_euler and lens at the shot start frames; (2) drive courier rotation and every subject keyframe from the embedded SHOT_SPEC numeric values (radians computed from value_start/value_end) instead of hardcoded constants, so the literal spec is the single source of truth; (3) add an explicit, AST-grammar-compatible means of excluding the drone from S01 visibility (or state precisely why the constraint is informational only) so the constraint text matches behavior; (4) confirm the dimension application path (primitive size and/or scale) is permitted by the grammar and yields the declared [0.8,0.6,1.8], [1.5,1.5,1.5], [1.2,1.2,0.4]; (5) resubmit the two artifacts with markers intact plus an updated continuation log, then run the supplied standalone AST/API checker and the scripted fallible review against the revised script and record their outcomes with their verification refs. No Blender execution will be claimed.
